A new global task is filed under its creator lane's project (the lane's
project membership, when it still belongs to the pane's running
process); a lane with no membership takes the `--parent` task's project
when it could have named that project itself. `--project NAME` files it
under a named project instead: your own, or one you hold a planner grant
for (the owner may name any; any other name is refused). `--no-project`
files it under none. A lane with global membership files unmapped tasks
unless it names a project.
A task that waits for something is BLOCKED with what it waits for, so
the next-job handoff skips it: `task block <id> --waiting-on owner |
evidence | release | numbers | task:<id> | pr:<repo>#<number>`
(`--reason` adds the detail). The kind is shown in `task read`,
`task list`, `task backlog` and `task_metrics`. `task:<id>` reopens
the task when that task completes, and `pr:<repo>#<number>` when
review-sync sees that pull request merged (if it closes without
merging the task stays blocked and gets a note). Every other wait is
cleared with `task unblock`.

`dunk-poll` is a small native client: one socket request returns status +
inbox count + unread messages + dunks (optionally panes/tasks). By default
the answer is compact: only the dunks that target the caller's pane (a
dunk records its target, not who created it), each without the text it
types, and `--tasks` rows reduced to id, status,
priority, scope, assignees and title. `--all` lists every dunk in the
fleet (still without text); `--full` returns everything the daemon sent.
A caller that shows the fleet's dunks (a sidebar, a status board) must

replacements.old:
Since 2.70.32 a batch is marked read only after the result is built, so a
read that fails no longer consumes the mail. A REPEATED batch after an error
is the fix working, not a bug: the same messages are offered again until a
read completes. `--peek` still marks nothing at all.
replacements.new:
A read prepares the complete response before atomically recording its read
marks, implicit acknowledgment and recovery receipt. Normal reads consume
the returned batch: no separate ack call is needed. Use `--no-ack` or
`inbox_read(ack=false)` for the previous explicit-ack workflow. A preparation
or write failure leaves the batch unread and the prior receipt intact. A
repeated batch after an error is safe redelivery, not a new message.
`--peek` still changes neither mail nor the recovery receipt.

replacements.old:
Recover follows the read rule, not the ack rule: like inbox read it is
permissive (inspecting a stranded mailbox is how the backlog gets drained),
while ack stays scoped to the caller's own mailbox.
replacements.new:
Recover and ack use the same mailbox authorization as read. Every role
that can read inbox mail, including planners, can recover and acknowledge
its own messages. Ordinary lanes cannot recover another lane's or the
human owner's mailbox. Existing privileged read access is unchanged.
After a lost read response, recover replays the latest batch even when the
normal read already acknowledged it. Empty reads preserve that receipt;
repeated recovery is safe, and a newer non-empty read replaces the one-batch
buffer. Existing retention and deletion bounds still apply. Explicit ack
is optional after normal reads and remains idempotent; it clears only the
named IDs from the receipt. In manual mode (`--no-ack` / `ack=false`), ack
only bodies you received and displayed; recover missing bodies first.
The messages-only default remains unchanged.

cleared with `task unblock`.

After pushing, a writer runs one command:
`dunkingsheep pr wait OWNER/REPO#PR --head FULL_SHA --author-task TASK_ID`.
Use the full pushed SHA and your currently claimed work task. The guarded daemon
records your authenticated process-bound lane and task for that exact PR head.
The first declaration binds that work task to its repository/PR; a mismatched
PR is refused without changes. Use one work task per PR.
Ordinary waiters, shared Git identities and editable PR-body text do not declare
authorship. Run the command again after each push. The first writer for a head
remains its primary author unless a coordinator records an audited correction;
co-authors accumulate, and every earlier contributor
remains excluded from reviewing the PR.

A process-bound planner with the repository/task project grant can correct an
attribution using `dunkingsheep pr correct-author OWNER/REPO#PR --head FULL_SHA
--author-task TASK_ID --author PANE --reason "explanation"` (one command).
Correction is CLI/socket-only and does not widen the grouped MCP schemas.
The named work task must be associated with the corrected writer. This is also
the explicit coordinator exception for rebinding a task to a different PR.
Contributors cannot correct their own PR, even after becoming a planner. The
audit retains old/new author and task bindings, planner and reason. Old/new
contributors remain excluded; conflicting live reviewer assignments/leases are
removed, and live unjudged review attribution is refreshed. Completed verdicts
and merge policy are unchanged. The distinct correction verb is refused by an
older daemon before writes. A writer client also requires a task-binding receipt;
an older declaration implementation cannot silently confirm the new guarantee.

Missing or stale head attribution still files an author-unknown review, without
automatic reviewer assignment. An unassigned author-unknown review cannot be
automatically claimed by a reviewer; the coordinator must route it first.
Its explicitly granted project coordinator gets
one inbox notice per PR, including across pushes and restarts. With no resolvable
coordinator, the task stays visible in `review list`; no recipient is guessed.
Review bodies and JSON list output show provenance; existing task announcements
carry it to reviewers. A recorded verdict sends an inbox notice to the author;
this is not a merge decision. Merge behavior is unchanged.

Authorship and notice receipts are additive tables. Older daemons can open the
store and perform ordinary task operations, but ignore newer authorship/correction records. After
rollback, route reviews manually to independently known reviewers until the
attribution-aware daemon returns. Retain the tables; never backfill from shared
Git identities. This is explicit work attribution, not proof of a GitHub push or
a new security boundary. If wait registration fails after declaration, authorship
remains recorded; retrying the same command is idempotent for authorship.

To address a proactive message to the human, use the reserved `owner` mailbox:
`dunkingsheep inbox send owner --subject 'Ready' 'The requested notice is ready.'`.
This appears in Your inbox as an agent message, linked to its recorded thread.
Addressing the VP's pane or lane name instead sends to the VP conversation.
A pane-less caller authenticated by an owner-role service token is attributed to
that token's registered label as an agent; it is never treated as human-origin.
Only an authenticated human reply promotes the whole thread into Your inbox.
The Inbox polls every five seconds; newly returned rows appear without reloading.
